ben: Strange one — sample app on emulator shows frequent timeouts for small health checks when a large file upload is in progress. Works fine on real devices and CI.
zoe: Emulator only? Any stack traces?
ben: Yes only on emulator. Logs show small GETs to /health queueing for tens of seconds while a single 50MB upload streams. OkHttp client seems to hold connections and new calls wait.
peter: Default OkHttp dispatcher has maxRequests=64 and maxRequestsPerHost=5. If upload uses persistent HTTP/2 stream, or the server treats emulator mapping 10.0.2.2 as same host, small calls can be queued behind active calls depending on connection reuse and multiplexing quirks.
ben: Here's the repro: Pixel 4 API 30 emulator, sample app using one shared OkHttpClient for uploads and other calls (Retrofit). Start a 50MB upload (streaming RequestBody), then quickly hit /health every second. On emulator health checks often block >15s and then fail with connect/read timeout. On device they complete instantly.
zoe: Could be dispatcher starvation or connection pool interaction. Which OkHttp version?
ben: OkHttp 4.9.3. Using default Dispatcher and ConnectionPool. No per-call timeouts set.
lina: Two mitigations: 1) use a dedicated OkHttpClient for long-running uploads with its own Dispatcher (higher maxRequestsPerHost) and ConnectionPool, 2) set per-call timeouts (callTimeout/connectTimeout/readTimeout) for health checks so they don't wait forever.
peter: Also note emulator networking via 10.0.2.2 sometimes collapses multiple virtual hosts, making per-host limits more aggressive. For the sample app we should show best-practice: create separate clients for foreground interactive calls vs background uploads. Example Kotlin snippet:
```
// interactive client for UI calls
val interactiveClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 64; maxRequestsPerHost = 8 })
  .callTimeout(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .build()

// upload client for heavy streaming
val uploadClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 8; maxRequestsPerHost = 2 })
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(8, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) // stream until done
  .build()
```
ben: I tried separating clients and the emulator health checks became stable.
zoe: For onboarding docs let's add: 1) guidance to avoid sharing a single OkHttpClient for interactive + heavy streaming workloads, 2) a note about emulator host mapping causing per-host limits to behave oddly, 3) sample code showing separate clients and per-call timeouts.
lina: Also add a small troubleshooting section in the Android quickstart: "If your UI calls stall while uploads are running on emulator, consider separate clients or increase maxRequestsPerHost for interactive client." Include a short FAQ entry.
peter: We should not recommend globally increasing maxRequestsPerHost without thinking about real server load. Prefer per-client tuning in sample apps.
ben: I'll open a PR with the sample app change (two clients), update the README with repro + workaround, and add a tiny integration test that uploads and asserts health checks stay under 1s.
devex-bot: Issue DEVEX-4427 created: "emulator: dispatcher/connection-pool starvation for shared OkHttpClient during streaming uploads" assigned to ben
ben: Thanks — will include logs and the exact emulator image in the PR. :shipit:
